title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Cellular Respiration
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 5 · 10 questions · 96 marks · 34 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question, and the paper, year and question number are in the Sources block at the foot of each one. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in that same block.

Do Cluster 1 first. Chemiosmosis, electron transport chains and reduced coenzymes are taught there in the chloroplast and repeated here in the mitochondrion. One outcome, 3(l), covers both organelles, so the second telling should feel like the same argument in a different compartment. Q5(f) asks you to state the difference in one mark.

Respiration carries the highest straight-recall share of any chapter measured in this Book, at 15.5%. Locations and products can be asked cold, and 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Q21 and Specimen Paper 3 Q1(a)(iv) are both nothing but that, for 7 marks between them. But the specimen never asked for the four stages. Specimen Paper 2 Q7 opened on one sentence and then asked for the role of one coenzyme, the consequence of removing oxygen, and chemiosmosis read off a figure. Function, not sequence.

The anchors. Question 5 is 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 7, parts (b), (c)(i) and (c)(ii), with the specimen's own Figure 7.1. Question 4(b) is Specimen Paper 2 Q7(a). Question 2(b) is Specimen Paper 3 Q1(a)(iv) at its real 6 marks. Question 6 is the full-cycle question: glycolysis through to oxidative phosphorylation, at its real 15 marks, on your own school's 2024 Paper 3.

Two MCQs. Q1(a) is Specimen Paper 1 Q21 word for word. Q4(a) is your own school's 2024 Paper 1 Q23, on which over 40% of the cohort chose an option containing "reduction of NAD occurs at the cristae". The paper awards one mark for the letter; the drill then makes you justify every option.

Cumulative over Books 1 to 4. Q3(b) needs the hydrophobic core and carrier-protein specificity from Book 1 membranes. Q3(c) needs the organelle inventory of a mature red blood cell. Q9 is a whole essay on membranes and cannot be answered without Book 1. Q10(b) needs the hydrogen-to-oxygen ratio of a triglyceride from Book 1 lipids. Say the Book 1 gap out loud when it surfaces.

What the marks reward. A scheme rejects a substrate being broken down or converted where it should be decarboxylated or oxidised. Schemes reject produce energy and synthesise energy outright. A scheme rejects ATP accounting given without consideration of stoichiometry, so every number carries its denominator. Write lactate, not lactic acid.

Do not quote a total ATP yield. LO 3(h) excludes it in writing and your own notes print two different totals twelve centimetres apart. Three real schemes in this drill award totals; each one is flagged in the answer as a point not to reproduce. Say almost 90% or the great majority of the ATP and move on.

One number you must get right: six carbon dioxide per glucose, not four. Two from the link reaction and four from the Krebs cycle. Your Overview page on 5.2 page 5 prints four; the same chapter's budget table on page 23 and its own boxed equation on page 5 both print six. Nothing in the syllabus excludes carbon dioxide output and LO 3(g) asks for products formed, so this is the one numerical error in Book 5 that is a genuine loss rather than a trap. Question 2(b) catches it.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not merely for duplicated labels. Q1 which compartment does what, read off protein density · Q2 the two matrix stages named and outlined, and the carbon dioxide budget · Q3 glycolysis at exactly outcome depth, and why its product cannot leave · Q4 the coenzymes as objects in their own right, apart from the pathway · Q5 the chain, the oxygen and the gradient, which is the specimen's own respiration anchor · Q6 the whole of aerobic respiration organised by feature · Q7 three different ways of breaking the same chain · Q8 what fermentation is actually for · Q9 membranes as the reason any of it works · Q10 substrates that are not glucose. Two shared marking points exist in the set and both are deliberate. Q6 is the synthesis question, so its list reaches across Q1 to Q5 by design. Q3(b) and Q9 both credit the hydrophobic core as a barrier to phosphorylated glucose; the paper set it as a three-mark Suggest in one place and as one sentence of a ten-mark essay in the other, which is exactly the difference in resolution worth rehearsing.

Nothing from Books 6 to 9, and nothing from Cluster 3. Respirometers, the respiratory quotient, soda lime, yeast dye methods, results-table layout and planning are Cluster 3. The named ETC complexes and carriers, the ATP synthase rotor mechanism, the ten glycolysis intermediates, phosphofructokinase regulation, the shuttle systems and every Krebs intermediate except oxaloacetate are excluded by the syllabus and appear nowhere in these questions except where a real stem supplies them.
